newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says monetary base to rise 24.5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says monetary base to rise 24.5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Banco de Mexico estimated Wednesday that monetary base would grow by about 24.5 percent in 1997 compared to its closing level at the end of 1996.
In a statement outlining its monetary programme for next year, the central bank also said it expected net international assets would increase by at least $1.9 billion in 1997.
Banco de Mexico said that its primary objective in monetary policy in 1997 was to help drive consumer inflation down to a level of 15 percent.
It also said it estimated real Gross Domestic Product growth of more than four percent next year.
The central bank said it would set quarterly objectives for variations in monetary base and net domestic credit for 1997 once it knew the closing level for monetary base in 1996.
